docs.title: vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template
docs.text:
vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template is a MkDocs plugin that lets you write Markdown inside the Jinja2 template files of your theme. You wrap the Markdown in a {% md %} ... {% mdend %} block, and the plugin converts it to HTML while MkDocs renders the page.

Theme templates are HTML. Your content is Markdown. Without the plugin, any text you put in a template override — an announcement bar, a footer note, a notice above every page — must be written as hand-made HTML. With the plugin, you write that text in the same Markdown you use for your pages.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Here is a template override with one Markdown block:

{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block announce %}
  {% md %}
  Version 2 is out. Read the **[upgrade notes]({{ base_url }}/upgrade/)**.
  {% mdend %}
{% endblock %}

When MkDocs renders a page with this template, three things happen in order:

  1. Jinja2 renders the block body. {{ base_url }} becomes the relative path to the site root: . on the home page, .. on a page one level down.
  2. The plugin removes the common leading indentation from the block, so the two-space indent does not turn the text into a Markdown code block.
  3. The plugin converts the text to HTML with the same Markdown extensions that your mkdocs.yml lists under markdown_extensions.

On a page one level down, the result is:

<p>Version 2 is out. Read the <strong><a href="../upgrade/">upgrade notes</a></strong>.</p>

The announcement bar at the top of this site is built this way. Its source is in Examples.

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• The tag pair is {% md %} to open and {% mdend %} to close.
  • The plugin has no configuration options. You enable it by name: markdown-in-template.
  • Template Markdown uses your site's markdown_extensions and their settings, so tables, admonitions and footnotes work the same way as in page bodies.
  • The plugin resets its Markdown converter before each block, so footnotes from one block do not appear in the next one.
  • The package needs Python 3.12 or later and MkDocs 1.5 or later.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: You do not call the plugin's Python API to use it; MkDocs does. This page is for contributors and for anyone who wants to reuse the Jinja2 extension outside MkDocs.

docs.title: __version__
docs.text:
from mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin import __version__

A string with the package version. At build time, hatch-vcs writes it into the generated module mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin/__version__.py from the Git tag. If that module does not exist, for example in an editable install made before the first build, __version__ is "0.0.0+local".

docs.title: class MarkdownInTemplatePlugin(BasePlugin)
docs.text:
The MkDocs plugin, registered under the name markdown-in-template.

config_scheme = () The plugin has no configuration options. on_env(env, config, files) -> Environment

MkDocs event handler. Stores config.get("markdown_extensions", []) and config.get("mdx_configs", {}) in env.globals, calls env.add_extension(MarkdownJinjaExtension), and returns the same env object.

Parameter Type Description env jinja2.Environment The theme's template environment. config mkdocs.config.Config The loaded site configuration. files mkdocs.structure.files.Files The site's files. Not used.

docs.title: class MarkdownJinjaExtension(Extension)
docs.text:
A Jinja2 extension that adds the {% md %} ... {% mdend %} block tag.

tags = {"md"} The tag names this extension handles. __init__(env)

Reads two globals from env and creates a markdown.Markdown instance:

Global Default Passed to markdown.Markdown as mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_markdown_extensions [] extensions mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_mdx_configs {} extension_configs

Stores the instance as self.markdowner and on the environment with env.extend(markdowner=...).

parse(parser) -> Node | list[Node] Called by Jinja2 for each {% md %} tag. Parses the body up to {% mdend %} and returns a jinja2.nodes.CallBlock that calls _render_markdown at render time. _render_markdown(caller) -> str Calls caller() to render the body, dedents it with _dedent, resets self.markdowner, and returns self.markdowner.convert(text). _dedent(text) -> str (static method) Returns textwrap.dedent(text.strip("\n")): blank lines at both ends are removed, then the common leading whitespace of all lines.

docs.title: Using the extension without MkDocs
docs.text:
The extension works in any Jinja2 environment. Set the two globals before you add it, because __init__ reads them:

from jinja2 import Environment

from mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin.plugin import MarkdownJinjaExtension

env = Environment()
env.globals["mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_markdown_extensions"] = ["tables"]
env.globals["mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_mdx_configs"] = {}
env.add_extension(MarkdownJinjaExtension)

template = env.from_string(
    "<main>\n"
    "  {% md %}\n"
    "  # {{ title }}\n"
    "\n"
    "  | Key | Value |\n"
    "  |-----|-------|\n"
    "  | a   | 1     |\n"
    "  {% mdend %}\n"
    "</main>"
)
print(template.render(title="Report"))

Output:

<main>
  <h1>Report</h1>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>a</td>
<td>1</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</main>

Without the globals, the extension uses no Markdown extensions, so tables and other extended syntax are not converted.

The _render_markdown and _dedent methods have a leading underscore. Treat them as internal: the tests call them directly, but their names and signatures may change.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The whole plugin is one module, mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin/plugin.py, with two classes. This page follows a build from start to end and shows where each class acts.

docs.title: The two classes
docs.text:
Class Base class Job MarkdownInTemplatePlugin mkdocs.plugins.BasePlugin Hooks into the MkDocs build and adds the Jinja2 extension to the theme environment. MarkdownJinjaExtension jinja2.ext.Extension Defines the md tag, captures the block body and converts it to HTML.

MkDocs finds the plugin class through the entry point declared in pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."mkdocs.plugins"]
markdown-in-template = "mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin.plugin:MarkdownInTemplatePlugin"

docs.title: Build sequence
docs.text:
mkdocs build
 │
 ├─ load mkdocs.yml ──────────────► markdown_extensions, mdx_configs
 ├─ convert every page's Markdown
 ├─ create the theme's Jinja2 environment
 ├─ on_env  (MarkdownInTemplatePlugin)
 │     ├─ env.globals[...markdown_extensions] = config["markdown_extensions"]
 │     ├─ env.globals[...mdx_configs]         = config["mdx_configs"]
 │     └─ env.add_extension(MarkdownJinjaExtension)
 │            └─ __init__: create one markdown.Markdown instance
 └─ render each page's template
       ├─ Jinja2 compiles templates; parse() turns {% md %}…{% mdend %} into a CallBlock
       └─ at render time: _render_markdown(caller)
             ├─ caller()      → body text, Jinja2 already applied
             ├─ _dedent()     → blank lines trimmed, common indent removed
             ├─ reset()       → converter state cleared
             └─ convert()     → HTML string inserted into the page

docs.title: Step 1: passing the Markdown settings to the extension
docs.text:
Jinja2 creates extension objects itself when you call env.add_extension(). The extension's constructor receives only the environment, not the MkDocs configuration. To get the site's Markdown settings into the extension, the plugin stores them in the environment globals first, under two keys:

  • mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_markdown_extensions
  • mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_mdx_configs

MarkdownJinjaExtension.__init__ reads both keys, with an empty list and an empty dict as defaults, and creates a markdown.Markdown object from them. It also attaches that object to the environment with env.extend(markdowner=...), so it is reachable as env.markdowner.

Because the values are globals, templates can also read them, for example {{ mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin_markdown_extensions }}. This is a side effect of the design, not a supported interface.

docs.title: Step 2: parsing the block
docs.text:
MarkdownJinjaExtension.tags is {"md"}, so Jinja2 calls the extension's parse() method when it meets {% md %}. The method:

  1. Reads the md token and remembers its line number.
  2. Parses everything up to {% mdend %} as normal template content, with parser.parse_statements(("name:mdend",), drop_needle=True).
  3. Returns a CallBlock node that calls _render_markdown with the parsed body.

Since the body is parsed as template content, it may contain any Jinja2 statements and expressions. They run when the template renders.

docs.title: Step 3: rendering the block
docs.text:
At render time, Jinja2 calls _render_markdown(caller). caller() renders the body and returns its text. Then:

  1. _dedent() calls textwrap.dedent(text.strip("\n")).
  2. self.markdowner.reset() clears per-document state such as footnotes and reference definitions.
  3. self.markdowner.convert(text) returns the HTML.

The returned string replaces the block in the template output.

docs.title: Design choices
docs.text:
One converter per build. The converter is created once, when the extension is added, and reused for every block. The source describes this as matching how MkDocs renders page bodies. The reset() call before each block makes reuse safe. Version 1.0.5 added that call; before it, footnotes leaked from one block into the next.

The site's extensions, not a separate list. Reusing markdown_extensions means template text renders like page text, and you configure extensions in one place. The trade-off is that you cannot give template blocks a different extension set.

No link rewriting. MkDocs rewrites relative links in page Markdown with processors it adds per page. The plugin's converter does not have those processors, so links in blocks are left as written.

docs.title: What the plugin does not do
docs.text:
• It does not read or change page Markdown. It only acts on templates.
  • It does not add template filters or global functions other than the two settings globals described above.
  • It does not cache the HTML of a block between pages. A block in main.html is converted again for every page.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The plugin has no options of its own. Its behaviour is controlled by three parts of mkdocs.yml that you already use: the plugins list, markdown_extensions, and theme.custom_dir.

docs.title: Plugin entry
docs.text:
plugins:
  - markdown-in-template

The plugin class defines an empty config_scheme, so it accepts no keys of its own. If you write one, for example:

plugins:
  - markdown-in-template:
      foo: false

MkDocs prints Plugin 'markdown-in-template' option 'foo': Unrecognised configuration name: foo. That is a warning in a normal build and stops the build with mkdocs build --strict.

docs.title: Turning the plugin off
docs.text:
MkDocs 1.6 accepts a generic enabled key for every plugin that does not define its own:

plugins:
  - markdown-in-template:
      enabled: false

With the plugin off, any template that contains {% md %} fails to compile. Disable the plugin only together with the templates that use it. MkDocs 1.5 has no generic enabled key; remove the plugin from the list instead.

docs.title: Position in the list
docs.text: The README recommends that you list the plugin early. The plugin acts in the on_env event. MkDocs fires it once per build, after it has converted the Markdown of every page and before it renders any page template. The block conversion then happens while each template renders. By the time other plugins see the page HTML, for example in on_post_page, the Markdown blocks are already HTML.

docs.title: Markdown extensions
docs.text:
Template Markdown is converted with the extensions in markdown_extensions and their settings. The plugin reads both values from the MkDocs configuration:

MkDocs config value What the plugin uses it for markdown_extensions The list of extensions passed to markdown.Markdown(extensions=...) mdx_configs The per-extension settings passed as extension_configs=...

mdx_configs is not a key you write. MkDocs builds it from the settings you put under each extension in markdown_extensions.

MkDocs always adds three extensions to the list, even if you do not name them: toc, tables and fenced_code. Template blocks therefore support tables and fenced code blocks, and their headings get id attributes, in every site.

For this configuration:

markdown_extensions:
  - admonition
  - toc:
      permalink: true

the plugin passes these values to Python-Markdown:

extensions = ["toc", "tables", "fenced_code", "admonition"]
extension_configs = {"toc": {"permalink": True}}

A heading in a template block then gets a ¶ permalink, the same as a heading in a page.

docs.title: Links in template blocks
docs.text: MkDocs rewrites links such as [Usage](usage.md) only in page Markdown. In a template block, links are converted as written. See Links and images for how to build working URLs.

docs.title: Theme overrides folder
docs.text:
To add a Markdown block to a theme, you override one of its templates. MkDocs reads overrides from theme.custom_dir:

theme:
  name: material
  custom_dir: overrides

The folder path is relative to mkdocs.yml. A file in it replaces the theme file with the same relative path. For example, overrides/main.html replaces the theme's main.html, and overrides/partials/footer.html replaces the theme's footer partial.

If you build a theme of your own, you can put {% md %} blocks directly in the theme's templates. The plugin must then be enabled in every site that uses the theme, or the templates fail to compile.

docs.title: Configuration of this site
docs.text:
This documentation site uses the plugin itself. The relevant parts of its src_docs/mkdocs.yml:

theme:
  name: materialx
  custom_dir: overrides
plugins:
  - search
  - markdown-in-template

src_docs/build.sh installs the plugin from the repository root with uvx ... --with .., so the site is always built with the current source.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This page explains how to set up the project, run the checks that CI runs, build the documentation and the package, and make a release.

Do not edit by hand. build.sh Builds the documentation and the package publish.sh Tags a release and uploads it to PyPI .github/workflows/ CI, documentation and release workflows

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Git, Python 3.12 or later, and optionally uv.

  1. Clone the repository with its tags. hatch-vcs needs the tags to compute the version.

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template
cd vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template

  2. Install the package in editable mode with the dev extra:

    pip install -e ".[dev]"

    The dev extra installs pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, mypy and types-Markdown.

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
These are the same commands that .github/workflows/ci.yml runs.

Check Command Tests pytest -v Tests with coverage pytest -v --cov=mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin --cov-report=term Lint ruff check . Formatting ruff format --check . Types mypy

Without an editable install, run the tests with uv:

uv run --with pytest pytest -q

docs.title: What the tests cover
docs.text:
tests/test_plugin.py contains:

  • test_dedent_strips_common_indentation and test_dedent_trims_surrounding_blank_lines for _dedent.
  • test_render_converts_markdown_to_html for basic conversion.
  • test_render_resets_between_blocks, which checks that a footnote from one block does not appear in the next.
  • test_on_env_registers_extension_and_copies_config for the plugin hook.
  • test_integration_mkdocs_build, which runs a real mkdocs build with a minimal theme whose main.html contains a {% md %} block.

CI runs the suite on Python 3.12 and 3.13, on Ubuntu and Windows, and in a separate job against MkDocs >=1.5,<1.6 and >=1.6,<2.0.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme. src_docs/build.sh runs both through uvx at pinned versions, and installs this repository with --with .. so that the site's own template override uses the current plugin code.

  1. Build into docs/:

    src_docs/build.sh

    The build runs in strict mode, so any warning stops it.

  2. Or start a live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

Edit the pages in src_docs/md/, never the HTML in docs/. On every push to main that changes src_docs/, the Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ and commits the result.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package

This removes dist/, runs uv build, and checks the result with uvx twine check dist/*. ./build.sh with no argument builds the documentation and the package. ./build.sh docs builds only the documentation.

The wheel contains only the mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin package. The sdist contains the package, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and LICENSE.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The version comes from Git tags through hatch-vcs. There is no version number in pyproject.toml. At build time, hatch-vcs writes mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin/__version__.py. That file is in .gitignore; do not commit it.

On a tagged commit with a clean tree, the version equals the tag without the v, for example 1.0.5. Between tags, it is a development version such as 1.0.6.dev3+g1a2b3c4.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
Releases go to PyPI as vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template.

  1. Add the changes to CHANGELOG.md.
  2. Set a PyPI token for uv, for example in UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.

  3. Run:

    ./publish.sh

publish.sh runs uvx gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes it. The script then checks that HEAD carries a vX.Y.Z tag, builds the package with ./build.sh package, and uploads dist/* with uv publish.

The pushed tag also starts .github/workflows/release.yml. That workflow builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with trusted publishing (skip-existing: true, so a version that publish.sh already uploaded is skipped), and creates a GitHub release with the matching CHANGELOG.md section.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Line length 100, target Python 3.12, checked by ruff with the rule sets E, F, I, UP, B and SIM.
  • Type hints on all functions; mypy checks the package.
  • Each source file starts with a this_file comment that gives its path.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Each example below is a complete template file. Put it in your custom_dir folder (see Configuration) at the path given in its heading. All examples were built with the plugin enabled.

docs.title: Announcement bar in MaterialX
docs.text:
This site shows a bar at the top of every page. Its source is src_docs/overrides/main.html in this repository:

{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block announce %}
  {% md %}
  This bar is Markdown in `src_docs/overrides/main.html`, rendered by the
  **markdown-in-template** plugin. [See how it is built]({{ base_url }}/examples/#announcement-bar-in-materialx).
  {% mdend %}
{% endblock %}

How it works:

  • announce is an empty block in the base.html of Material for MkDocs and MaterialX. The theme shows the announcement bar only when the block has content.
  • {{ base_url }} makes the link work from every page, because Jinja2 replaces it with the relative path to the site root before the Markdown is converted.
  • The backticks and asterisks become <code> and <strong>, as in a page.

docs.title: Notice from page front matter
docs.text:
File: overrides/main.html

This override shows a note above the content of any page whose front matter has a notice key.

{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {% if page.meta.notice %}
    {% md %}
    !!! note
        {{ page.meta.notice }}
    {% mdend %}
  {% endif %}
  {{ super() }}
{% endblock %}

A page that uses it:

---
notice: "This page describes the **1.x** API. See [2.x](https://example.com/2/)."
---
# API

The rendered note:

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This page describes the <strong>1.x</strong> API. See <a href="https://example.com/2/">2.x</a>.</p>
</div>

The front matter value is plain text, but because it goes through the Markdown block, the **1.x** and the link are rendered. The !!! note line needs the admonition extension in markdown_extensions.

docs.title: Footer text with a licence link
docs.text:
File: overrides/partials/copyright.html

Material for MkDocs prints config.copyright in the footer as-is. This override writes the footer line in Markdown and adds a licence link:

<div class="md-copyright">
  {% md %}
  {{ config.copyright }} Licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
  Built with [MkDocs](https://www.mkdocs.org/) and *markdown-in-template*.
  {% mdend %}
</div>

With copyright: "Copyright © 2026 Example Ltd." in mkdocs.yml, the footer contains:

<div class="md-copyright">
  <p>Copyright © 2026 Example Ltd. Licensed under <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>.
Built with <a href="https://www.mkdocs.org/">MkDocs</a> and <em>markdown-in-template</em>.</p>
</div>

Replacing partials/copyright.html removes the theme's own "Made with" line, because your file replaces the whole partial.

docs.title: Shared text in an included partial
docs.text:
Files: overrides/main.html and overrides/partials/support.html

A block works in a partial that another template includes. This lets you keep reusable Markdown in one file.

overrides/partials/support.html:

{% md %}
---

Questions? Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/example/project/issues)[^1].

[^1]: You need a GitHub account.
{% mdend %}

overrides/main.html:

{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}
  {% include "partials/support.html" %}
{% endblock %}

The footnote renders as a normal footnote list under the paragraph, because footnotes is in markdown_extensions. The footnote ids (fn:1, fnref:1) are computed for the block alone. If the page body also has a footnote 1, the page contains the same ids twice and the links jump to the first one. Use a named footnote such as [^support] in templates to avoid the clash.

docs.title: Minimal theme template
docs.text:
File: theme/main.html, with theme: {name: null, custom_dir: theme}

The plugin does not depend on any theme. The project's integration test builds a site whose only template is this file:

<!doctype html><html><body>
{% md %}
# Injected

Regular and **bold** text.
{% mdend %}
</body></html>

The built index.html contains <h1 id="injected">Injected</h1> and <strong>bold</strong>.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The plugin is a regular Python package. You install it into the same Python environment that runs MkDocs, then enable it in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Version Source of the requirement Python 3.12 or later requires-python in pyproject.toml MkDocs 1.5.0 or later dependencies in pyproject.toml Jinja2 3.0.3 or later dependencies in pyproject.toml Markdown 3.3.6 or later dependencies in pyproject.toml

The CI workflow runs the test suite on Python 3.12 and 3.13, on Linux and Windows. A separate job runs it on Linux with Python 3.12 against MkDocs 1.5.x and 1.6.x.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
The distribution name is vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template. The import name is mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin. The plugin name you use in mkdocs.yml is markdown-in-template.

pipuvFrom GitHubOne-off build with uvx 
pip install vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template

uv add vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template

pip install "git+https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template"

uvx --from mkdocs --with vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template mkdocs build

If you install from a local clone, use an editable install so that code changes take effect without reinstalling:

git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template
cd vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template
pip install -e .

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
1. Print the package version:

    python -c "import mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin as m; print(m.__version__)"

    The version comes from the Git tag through hatch-vcs, for example 1.0.5. An editable install made before the version file was generated prints 0.0.0+local.

  2. Confirm that MkDocs can see the plugin entry point:

    python -c "from importlib.metadata import entry_points; print([e.name for e in entry_points(group='mkdocs.plugins')])"

    The list contains markdown-in-template.

docs.title: Enable the plugin
docs.text:
Add the plugin to the plugins list in mkdocs.yml:

plugins:
  - search
  - markdown-in-template

Keep the search plugin

When you define plugins in mkdocs.yml, MkDocs no longer adds the default search plugin for you. List search again if you want site search.

The plugin has no options. See Configuration for the settings that do change how template Markdown renders.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
pip uninstall vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template

Remove markdown-in-template from plugins at the same time. Any template that still contains {% md %} then fails with TemplateSyntaxError: Encountered unknown tag 'md'.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walkthrough adds a Markdown notice above the content of every page in a site that uses Material for MkDocs. It takes about five minutes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • A MkDocs project with an mkdocs.yml and a docs/ folder.
  • The mkdocs-material theme installed, or another theme that lets you override templates (see step 6).
  • The plugin installed (see Installation).

docs.title: 1. Enable the plugin
docs.text:
Open mkdocs.yml and add markdown-in-template to plugins:

plugins:
  - search
  - markdown-in-template

docs.title: 2. Point the theme at an overrides folder
docs.text:
MkDocs looks for template overrides in the folder named by theme.custom_dir. The path is relative to mkdocs.yml.

theme:
  name: material
  custom_dir: overrides

Create the folder next to mkdocs.yml:

mkdir overrides

docs.title: 3. Write a Markdown block in a template
docs.text:
Create overrides/main.html with this content:

{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {% md %}
  !!! info "Draft"
      This page belongs to the **{{ config.site_name }}** draft.
      Send corrections to the [issue tracker](https://example.com/issues).
  {% mdend %}
  {{ super() }}
{% endblock %}

What each part does:

  • {% extends "base.html" %} keeps the theme's own layout.
  • {% block content %} replaces the page content block. {{ super() }} puts the original page content back after your notice.
  • {% md %} and {% mdend %} mark the text that the plugin converts from Markdown to HTML.
  • {{ config.site_name }} is a normal Jinja2 expression. Jinja2 fills it in before the plugin converts the block.
  • !!! info is an admonition. It renders only if admonition is in your markdown_extensions (step 4).

docs.title: 4. Enable the Markdown extensions the block uses
docs.text:
The block is converted with the extensions listed in mkdocs.yml. Add admonition so the !!! info line works:

markdown_extensions:
  - admonition

docs.title: 5. Build and check the result
docs.text:
1. Build the site:

    mkdocs build

  2. Open site/index.html in a browser.

Every page now starts with a "Draft" info box that contains the site name and a link. In the HTML source, the box is a <div class="admonition info"> element, the same markup MkDocs produces for an admonition in a page body.

docs.title: 6. Use another theme
docs.text: The plugin works with any theme, because it adds a tag to the Jinja2 environment rather than changing a theme. What differs between themes is the name of the template blocks you can override. Look in the theme's base.html or main.html for {% block ... %} names. For example, the built-in mkdocs theme has a content block in base.html.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Learn the indentation and nesting rules in Usage.
  • Copy more overrides from Examples.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Each entry gives the symptom you see, the cause, and the fix.

docs.title: "Encountered unknown tag 'md'"
docs.text:
The build stops with:

jinja2.exceptions.TemplateSyntaxError: Encountered unknown tag 'md'.

Cause: a template contains {% md %}, but the Jinja2 environment has no extension for it. The plugin is not active.

Fix:

  1. Check that markdown-in-template is in the plugins list of the mkdocs.yml you are building, and that it does not have enabled: false.

  2. Check that the package is installed in the Python environment that runs mkdocs:

    python -c "import mkdocs_markdown_in_template_plugin"

    If you build with uvx or pipx, the package must be added to that tool's environment, for example with uvx --from mkdocs --with vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template mkdocs build.

docs.title: "Jinja was looking for the following tags: 'mdend'"
docs.text:
The build stops with:

jinja2.exceptions.TemplateSyntaxError: Unexpected end of template. Jinja was looking for the following tags: 'mdend'. The innermost block that needs to be closed is 'md'.

Cause: a {% md %} block has no closing tag, or the closing tag is misspelled. The closing tag is {% mdend %}, not {% endmd %}.

Fix: add or correct the closing tag. The error message shows the template line where the open block starts.

docs.title: "The block renders as a code block"
docs.text:
The Markdown appears inside <pre><code> instead of as formatted text.

Cause: after dedenting, the text still starts with four or more spaces. This happens when one line of the block is indented less than the others, or when the block mixes tabs and spaces. The dedent step removes only the indentation that all non-blank lines share.

Fix: indent every line of the block by at least the same amount, using spaces only. Lines that are part of nested structures, such as an admonition body, should be indented further than the baseline, not less.

docs.title: "The Markdown is shown literally, not converted"
docs.text:
You see **bold** or # Heading as text in the built page.

Cause: the text is outside a {% md %} block, or in a template file that your theme does not use. A common case: you edited a copy of a template outside custom_dir, or the file name does not match the theme file it should replace.

Fix: check that the file is in the folder named by theme.custom_dir, at the same relative path as the theme file it replaces.

docs.title: "Admonitions, tables or footnotes are not rendered"
docs.text:
You see !!! note as a paragraph, or a footnote marker stays as [^1].

Cause: template blocks use only the extensions in markdown_extensions. Tables are always available, because MkDocs always loads tables. Admonitions need admonition, footnotes need footnotes.

Fix: add the extension to markdown_extensions in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: "A link in a template block is broken"
docs.text:
A link such as [Guide](guide.md) leads to a 404 page.

Cause: MkDocs rewrites .md links only in page Markdown. In a template block, the link stays guide.md.

Fix: build the URL with Jinja2, relative to the site root:

{% md %}
[Guide]({{ base_url }}/guide/)
{% mdend %}

docs.title: "Duplicate ids on the page"
docs.text:
An HTML validator reports duplicate id attributes, or a permalink or footnote link jumps to the wrong place.

Cause: headings and footnotes in a template block get ids computed from the block alone. If the page body has a heading with the same text, or a footnote with the same number, the ids are the same.

Fix: in templates, use heading text that does not appear in pages, and use named footnotes such as [^support].

docs.title: "Text from a Jinja2 variable changes the formatting"
docs.text:
A page title or front matter value with *, _ or # changes the formatting of the block.

Cause: Jinja2 inserts the variable before the Markdown is converted, and the plugin does not escape it. Markdown then reads the characters as syntax.

Fix: put the variable outside the {% md %} block, or escape the characters in the source value with a backslash.

docs.title: Getting more help
docs.text: If none of these entries matches, open an issue at https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-markdown-in-template/issues. Include the template that contains the block, the markdown_extensions and plugins sections of mkdocs.yml, and the full error message.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: This page describes the {% md %} block: where you can use it, what happens to the text inside it, and which rules it follows.

docs.title: Block syntax
docs.text:
A Markdown block starts with {% md %} and ends with {% mdend %}:

{% md %}
Markdown text
{% mdend %}

The tag takes no arguments. The closing tag is mdend, not endmd.

You can use the block in any template that MkDocs renders with the theme's Jinja2 environment:

  • main.html and other templates in your custom_dir
  • partials pulled in with {% include %}
  • inside {% block %} overrides of a parent template
  • inside {% if %} and {% for %} statements

docs.title: Processing order
docs.text:
For each block, at the moment the template renders, the plugin does this:

  1. Jinja2 renders the body. Variables, filters, {% if %} tests and loops inside the block run first. The plugin receives plain text.
  2. The text is dedented. Blank lines at the start and end are removed, and the indentation common to all lines is stripped.
  3. The Markdown converter is reset. State from the previous block, such as footnotes and reference links, is cleared.
  4. The text is converted to HTML with the site's Markdown extensions.
  5. The HTML replaces the block in the template output.

Follow one block through these steps. The template contains:

<footer>
    {% md %}
    Built with **{{ config.site_name }}**.
    {% mdend %}
</footer>

With site_name: Demo, step 1 produces "\n Built with **Demo**.\n ". Step 2 turns it into Built with **Demo**.. Step 4 produces:

<p>Built with <strong>Demo</strong>.</p>

docs.title: Indentation
docs.text:
Template files are usually indented to show the HTML structure. In Markdown, four spaces of indentation start a code block. To let you indent freely, the plugin removes the indentation that all lines of the block share.

The baseline is the common indentation of the non-blank lines. After leading blank lines are removed, the first line of text is usually where that baseline shows. Lines indented further than the baseline keep their extra indentation, so nested lists and admonition bodies still work:

<div class="notice">
    {% md %}
    !!! warning
        Indented by four more spaces: this is the admonition body.

    - item
        - nested item
    {% mdend %}
</div>

Mixed tabs and spaces

The dedent step uses Python's textwrap.dedent. It treats a tab and spaces as different characters, so a block that mixes them may keep its indentation and render as a code block. Use spaces in templates that contain Markdown blocks.

docs.title: Jinja2 inside the block
docs.text:
Because Jinja2 renders the body before conversion, you can build Markdown from template data:

{% if page.parent %}
{% md %}
## Pages in this section

{% for nav_item in page.parent.children %}
- [{{ nav_item.title }}]({{ nav_item.url | url }})
{%- endfor %}
{% mdend %}
{% endif %}

The - in {%- endfor %} removes the newline at the end of each loop pass. Without it, the loop leaves a blank line between items, and Markdown renders a loose list with every item wrapped in <p>.

Two consequences follow:

  • Text that Jinja2 outputs is not escaped by the plugin. If a variable contains * or _, Markdown reads those characters as formatting.
  • Jinja2 syntax in the block is never shown literally. To print {{ in the output, use Jinja2's own escaping, such as {{ '{{' }} or a {% raw %} ... {% endraw %} section.

docs.title: Links and images
docs.text:
Page Markdown and template Markdown handle links differently:

  • In a page, MkDocs rewrites a link such as [Usage](usage.md) to the URL of the built page.
  • In a template block, the plugin converts the link as written. usage.md stays usage.md in the HTML, which is a broken link on the built site.

In template blocks, build URLs with Jinja2 instead:

{% md %}
[Read the usage guide]({{ base_url }}/usage/)
{% mdend %}

base_url is the relative path from the current page to the site root. For paths to files in docs/, MkDocs also provides the url filter, for example {{ 'assets/logo.png' | url }}.

docs.title: Headings and anchors
docs.text:
If toc is active (MkDocs always loads it), a heading in a block gets an id attribute, and a permalink if toc is configured with permalink: true. The id is computed from the block alone. A heading with the same text in the page body gets the same id, so the page then contains a duplicate id. Use different heading text in templates, or use bold text instead of a heading.

Headings in a template block do not appear in the page's table of contents. The table of contents comes from the page body.

docs.title: Several blocks on one page
docs.text: A template can contain any number of blocks. Each block is converted on its own. The converter is reset before each block, so a footnote defined in one block is not printed again under the next one. A footnote reference and its definition must be in the same block.
